title: The Friday sermon
hookLine: two sermons before the Friday prayer, listened to in silence

cards: Medina, a Friday. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is standing and speaking to the people. Then a noise from the edge of town: a trade caravan has arrived, with goods to buy and the clamor of a market day.
A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says people got up and went, and only a few stayed seated. The Qur'an kept the moment.
In Pickthall's translation: "But when they spy some merchandise or pastime they break away to it and leave thee standing." The caravans are smaller now. They fit in a pocket, and they buzz.

teach.b: Khutbah means a sermon, an address. On Friday, the congregational prayer called jumu'ah is preceded by one; you met it in year two, with leave trade for a while. First, its shape.

Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet gave two sermons on Friday and sat briefly between them. So the imam stands, speaks, sits a moment, stands again, speaks again, and only then the prayer begins. Second, the call.
Eight days ago this path heard surah sixty-two's command to haste unto remembrance of Allah when the call is heard.

In Pickthall's translation the verse goes on: "and leave your trading." The same surah that keeps the caravan story tells people, two verses earlier, to put the market down when the call comes. Third, the silence.
A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says that if you tell the person beside you to be quiet while the imam is speaking, you yourself have spoken idly.
Even the shush counts. You listen, and let the person beside you do their own listening. Fourth, what the silence is for.
The congregation hears a person speak to them about this week, this city, these lives. Some of it lands, some doesn't.
The command is the same either way: the market waits, the shush waits, the phone waits.

teach.h: BETTER THAN PASTIME AND THAN MERCHANDISE.
teach.b: The caravan story ends with a line that answers it, in Pickthall's words: "That which Allah hath is better than pastime and than merchandise."

how: Each Friday at midday, Muslims gather at the mosque for jumu'ah: the imam gives two sermons with a short sit between them, the congregation listens in silence, and then they pray together.

games.q: you're in the mosque in Medina on a Friday, mid-sermon. a trade caravan arrives, with goods and the noise of a market. what do many of the people do?
o: get up and go to the market.
ask for the sermon to be shortened.
games.why: they went. the Qur'an kept it: "they break away to it and leave thee standing" (62:11), and answers that what is with God is better than merchandise.

practice: Put your phone out of reach, or face-down and silent if this lesson is playing on it, and listen to the room: the hum of something electric, a car outside, your own breath, without naming or judging any of it.

If you attend the Friday prayer, you can leave the phone off or in the car this week and give the khutbah your whole hearing. If you don't, give one person a conversation with no screen anywhere in it.

wordCard.voice: Khutbah. The sermon: on Friday, two addresses before the prayer, heard in a silence so full it leaves no room even for shushing. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: an address or sermon, given before the Friday prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: silence for the khutbah. The market, the shush and the phone can all wait. Back tomorrow, same hill.
